toll_basis.note: Tolls are round trip at New York E-ZPass rates (a tag issued by the New York E-ZPass service center), weekend off-peak. An E-ZPass tag from New Jersey, Connecticut or any other state pays the higher Tolls by Mail rate at MTA bridges and tunnels (for example $12.03 instead of $7.46 at the Whitestone, Throgs Neck, RFK and Verrazzano bridges). That figure is given beside each toll as the mail rate. Where a route enters the Manhattan congestion zone, no mail rate for the zone was found on a page that could be read, so the mail figure there is given as 'at least' the sum of the other crossings. Resident discounts are not applied.

An asterisk on the rent means a special offer applies. The rent terms say what it is.
Where a floor was read from the apartment number, the listing page does not state it. Confirm it on the tour.
For a few towns no police agency publishes a crime rate for the town alone. There, the rule that nothing shown has more crime than Jamaica could not be tested, and the page says so.
A parking fee counts as published only when the building's own page or a listing states it. A figure from a resident's review is an estimate and is labelled as one.
An apartment with an asterisk has one thing still to confirm: the elevator, whether dogs are allowed, or whether the listing is real and available. The text beside it says what and why.

Some things are worth knowing and never remove an apartment: a floor that is not published, a price quoted for a lease that is not 12 months, a cost that could pass $3,000 once parking and fees are known, a price that already has free months averaged in (only where the listing says so), a special offer (ask what a normal month costs), a condo rented by its owner, a dog weight limit with no number, and a town rule that restricts overnight street parking where the building's parking is not confirmed.
Pet rent is always counted. Where a building does not publish it, the cost uses an estimate, the median of the known pet rents in the same state, and it is marked as an estimate.

Where a building does not publish its parking fee or its required fees, a second figure adds the median of the known ones. It is shown beside the total with utilities and fees and is never used for the $3,000 limit.
Experience and neighborhood figures (medians and ranges) are computed over the apartments shown on the page. A neighborhood's distances from the door are those of its median building.
Where an elevator is named only on a listing site, in its amenity list or its text, it has not been confirmed on the building's own page.
Each apartment carries the date its price was read.
Cost lines that are not published add nothing to the total with utilities and fees. Each receipt names them as not published.

parking_rules.quote: Residents and businesses wishing to park a vehicle on the street in Residential Permit Parking Program areas require a permit

parking_rules.summary: Tenants need proof of residence plus a valid vehicle registration and driver's license; one accepted proof is a license and registration showing the New Brunswick address. Rules for a registration in a different name or address are on the page (extra documents).
parking_rules.quote: Along with your proof of residence you need valid vehicle registration and valid driver's license.

parking_rules.summary: Visitor permits are obtained online by the tenants of the dwelling, with the same proofs as a tenant permit.
parking_rules.quote: Visitor Permits must be obtained by the tenants of the dwelling online on the digital permits site.

parking_rules.summary: Alternate side parking for street sweeping runs from about April 1 to October 31.
parking_rules.quote: Alternate side parking regulations are in effect on or about April 1 to October 31.

parking_rules.summary: Parking is banned on certain posted streets whenever snow covers the roadway.
parking_rules.quote: Parking is prohibited on certain posted streets whenever snow has fallen and the accumulation covers the roadway.

parking_rules.summary: Downtown meters run 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. Monday to Saturday (some streets also 1-10 p.m. Sundays); $2.00 an hour for the first two hours, rising after.
parking_rules.quote: 1-2 hours: $2.00/hour Third hour: $3.00 Fourth hour: $4.00 Fifth hour: $5.00 Sixth hour: $6.00 Seventh hour: $7.00 Eighth hour: $8.00 8 hour Maximum Stay - 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. Monday through Saturday

parking_rules.summary: Parking Authority decks sell monthly parking: $200 a month at Lower Church Street, Morris Street and New Street decks; $210 at Gateway, NBPAC, Paterson Street, Plum Street and Wellness Plaza decks.
parking_rules.quote: Lower Church Street Deck ($200 per month) Morris Street Deck ($200 per month) New Street Deck ($200 per month) Gateway Deck ($210 per month)

safety.geography: Newark Police Department: serves Newark city, population 319,000

voices.excerpt: I do believe that it is less safe than some other cities but honestly, no where in America is completely safe.
Another major concern is the lack of adequate parking. Finding a parking space is consistently frustrating and inconvenient, especially when returning home after a long day.
That being said, there is obvious growth, and the people are doing their best with what they have. It has a lot of opportunity, beautiful architecture, and nice parks.
But there are select few places that will move you, like views downtown during a sunset. I love the city skyline downtown, I also love the food and cultural diversity.
There were moments when the city felt loud and intimidating, and adjusting to a new environment wasn’t easy.
Similar to NYC, without all the crowdedness and expensive prices.

Being a resident here since I was little, I was able to find a community within my own home, one that provides fun and an abundance of shared laughs whilst also making sure people get the education needed.

For the amount of money residents pay, basic expectations such as a clean, odor-free environment and reasonable parking accommodations should be met. I would not recommend living here based on my experience.
I love my city for how convenient it is everything is 15 minutes to 1 hour away from Major cities like NYC or Philly.
As a young woman, walking around alone often feels unsafe and anxiety-inducing—I almost never do it.
What I really like about Newark is its diversity—you can meet people from all over the world, and that brings a lot of culture, different perspectives, and good food!
It very hectic in the morning times and calm during the night.
I hope that in the future, this problem is solved and my community is much better.

safety.geography: Rahway Police Department: serves Rahway city, population 31,000

parking_rules.summary: Residential parking permits are free from the Rahway Parking Utility, 67 Lewis St (the downtown deck); permit holders can also get visitor permits. They apply only to the time-limited street you live on.

parking_rules.summary: A resident permit needs a valid NJ driver's license, permanent vehicle registration and insurance card, all showing the address of the street applied for; no other ID is accepted, so an out-of-state license or registration does not qualify.
parking_rules.quote: All three (3) must have the address of the street for which you are applying. The Division of Parking will not accept any other forms of ID.

parking_rules.summary: Monthly parking is sold by the Rahway Parking Utility (732-827-2222); there is a waitlist. Price not on the page.
parking_rules.quote: Please note, there is a waitlist for monthly parking permits

parking_rules.summary: On a snow emergency street you must move your car when significant snow is expected; use off-street parking where possible.
parking_rules.quote: If you live on a snow emergency street, you must remove your vehicle to provide access for emergency vehicles.

parking_rules.summary: Streets are swept once a week from April 1 through October. Whether cars must move is not stated.
parking_rules.quote: Street sweeping is done once per week from April 1st through October weather permitting.

dog_rules.summary: Dogs are licensed yearly: $10 spayed/neutered, $20 if not; $5 late fee from March 1.
dog_rules.quote: Spayed/Neutered $10.00 Not Spayed/Neutered: $20.00 Service Animal: No Fee

dog_rules.summary: The city asks owners to pick up after pets; bag dispensers are on Central Avenue by the Community Garden and at Mione Park on New Church Street.
dog_rules.quote: The City of Rahway has installed pet waste bag dispensers on Central Avenue by the Rahway Community Garden and at Mione Park on New Church Street

parking_rules.summary: Many NYC streets have alternate side parking (ASP) for street cleaning; days and hours are on the signs for each block. You cannot park on the side being cleaned for the whole posted time, even after the sweeper has passed.
parking_rules.quote: You cannot park on the side of the street that is being cleaned when ASP rules are in effect. The rules apply for the length of the entire block, and for the entire time posted on the sign, even if the street sweeper has already passed.

parking_rules.summary: ASP is not in effect on Sundays, and is suspended on listed legal and religious holidays, in severe weather and in emergencies.
parking_rules.quote: ASP rules are suspended on certain legal and religious holidays each year, during severe weather, and for emergencies. On Sundays, ASP is not in effect

parking_rules.summary: The city may suspend ASP for snow or emergencies, sometimes announced late in the day; ASP is restored after a snowfall so plows can clear the curb lane. No citywide snow-route parking ban was found on the pages read.
parking_rules.quote: NYC may suspend ASP regulations because of inclement weather or emergencies. The decision is sometimes made late in the day since weather patterns can change fast. NYC restores ASP regulations after a snowfall.

parking_rules.summary: No citywide overnight street-parking ban appears on NYC DOT's parking pages; what applies is whatever the signs on the block say, and the most restrictive sign wins.
parking_rules.quote: If there is more than one sign posted for the same area, the more restrictive one is the one in effect. If a sign is missing on a block, the remaining posted regulations are the ones that are in effect. Please check the entire block and read all signs carefully before you park.

parking_rules.summary: All of NYC is a tow-away zone: a car parked illegally, or with a missing or expired registration or inspection sticker, may be towed.
parking_rules.quote: All of New York City is a designated Tow Away Zone under the State's Vehicle and Traffic Law. This means that any vehicle parked or operated illegally, or with missing or expired registration or inspection stickers, may be towed.

parking_rules.summary: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.
parking_rules.quote: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of either side of a fire hydrant

parking_rules.summary: Meters are not in effect on Sundays or on the six major legal holidays. Other hours are on the meter or sign.
parking_rules.quote: Metered regulations are not in effect on Sundays nor major legal holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day).

parking_rules.summary: Passenger meter rates outside Manhattan's core: $2.50 first hour and $5.00 second hour in business districts such as Downtown Flushing and Jamaica; $2.00 / $3.00 in neighborhood retail districts; $1.50 / $2.50 elsewhere.
parking_rules.quote: Zone 1 - Business Districts outside of Manhattan (e.g., Downtown Brooklyn, Downtown Flushing, and Jamaica; Manhattan 125th Street) $2.50 $5.00 Zone 2 - Neighborhood Retail Districts $2.00 $3.00 Zone 3 - All Other Metered Locations $1.50 $2.50

parking_rules.summary: NYC DOT garages sell monthly permits: Court Square (Queens) $400, Borough Hall (Brooklyn) $330, Bay Ridge $275, Jerome-190th Street (Bronx) $250, Delancey and Essex (Manhattan) $600. No monthly rate is listed for the Queens Family Court garage in Jamaica.
Monthly garage permits are reserved online, first come first served, from five days before the month starts; a New York State driver's license check is run at reservation.
parking_rules.quote: Reservations open on the website five days before the first of the month at 10 am. All reservations are made for the upcoming month, on a first-come, first-served basis. A New York State Department of Motor Vehicles driver's license check is performed at the time of the reservation.

parking_rules.summary: Municipal parking fields (open lots) do not allow overnight parking; they close at the posted hour, typically 10 PM.
parking_rules.quote: Municipal parking fields do not allow overnight parking. The fields close as shown in the posted regulations for each facility. Parking after posted hours may result in a summons and leaves the vehicle at risk as there is no security at the closed facilities.

parking_rules.summary: Quarterly permits at municipal parking fields: Flushing #4 $300, Steinway #1 (Astoria) $500, Bayside $500, Brighton Beach $625, Sheepshead Bay #1 $300, Canarsie $300, Bronxdale $400.
parking_rules.quote: Bronxdale Municipal Parking Field $400 Bensonhurst #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Brighton Beach Municipal Parking Field $625 Canarsie Municipal Parking Field $300 Sheepshead Bay #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Bayside Municipal Parking Field $500 Flushing #4 Municipal Parking Field $300 Steinway #1 Municipal Parking Field $500

dog_rules.summary: Every dog in NYC must be licensed and wear the tag in public. A license costs $8.50 a year for a spayed or neutered dog; $34 for an unaltered dog over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: All dogs in New York City must have licenses, and the licenses must be attached to their collars while in public.

dog_rules.summary: License fee: $8.50 a year if spayed or neutered; if not, $8.50 under 4 months old and $34 over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: Licenses for spayed or neutered dogs of any age cost $8.50 per year. If your dog is not spayed or neutered, a license will cost $8.50 if the dog is under 4 months old, or $34 if it is older than 4 months.

dog_rules.summary: In any public place a dog must be on a leash no longer than six feet.
dog_rules.quote: a person who owns, possesses or controls a dog shall not permit it to be in any public place or in any open or unfenced area abutting on a public place unless the dog is effectively restrained by a leash or other restraint not more than six feet long.

dog_rules.summary: In city parks dogs must be leashed except where Parks rules allow off-leash; the Health Code lets Parks allow off-leash in unenclosed areas only within a window that starts no earlier than 9 PM and ends by 9 AM. The Parks rules themselves could not be read (site bot-walled).
dog_rules.quote: Such rules shall include provisions that prohibit unrestrained dogs in unenclosed DOPR controlled areas and facilities except during a specified range of time, that shall not begin earlier than 9:00 P.M. and not extend past 9:00 A.M.

dog_rules.summary: With proof of a current license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash in NYC Parks dog runs. The open-data list has 95 active runs (14 in Queens, 20 Brooklyn, 41 Manhattan, 15 Bronx, 5 Staten Island); see dog_parks.csv.
dog_rules.quote: With proof of current dog license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash at New York City park dog runs

dog_rules.summary: Owners must pick up after their dog in all public areas; the fine is up to $250.
dog_rules.quote: If you do not clean up after your dog, you may be fined up to $250.

voices.excerpt: Having spent my childhood and teenage years in Haverstraw, New York, I can say that there are areas of improvement when it comes to traffic congestion, limited education and safety protocols within the streets of center of Haverstraw in town

voices.excerpt: I personally love living in Haverstraw. I am surrounded by lively people who light up the sky at night (not literally).

Housing is affordable, it's located on the Hudson River. Things that need to change include education geared toward the community's youth regarding STD's as the rates are higher then the national average.
Property tax is extremely high for what the average income is of the residents.

voices.excerpt: There has been more crime accurately been happening a bit more often then usual, I've been assaulted, there's been gang activity's, mostly at night, and overall the area has been increasing with areas being more polluted.
If there was something I would change it would be the limited parking spaces due to construction.

There are great mom-and-pop coffee shops and restaurants that I love. We are also next to two train stations so travel is reliable.

If there had to be any change (which I am not sure how to change this), I think the loudness in the Summer. It’s the neighborhood that logs more noise complaints each summer than any place in the 5 boroughs.
Sure you save on rent but you have almost an hour commute to get anywhere, you lose so much sleep and peace of mind, it’s really NOT worth it.

I love the neighborhood and sense of community, especially since it's more separate than the rest of Manhattan and feels like its own little city, but commuting to lower Manhattan is still pretty easy and convenient.

voices.excerpt: The expansive park offers an array of recreational activities, from picnics to hiking and biking trails. Whether you're a nature enthusiast or just looking for a peaceful escape, Forest Park is the perfect retreat.
It is a friendly and quiet neighborhood. A lot of new shops and restaurants are opening up nearby.
Too many loud cars racing, drifting between apartment buildings, fireworks every night over 2 years now.
I feel that the people are much more down-to-earth here compared to some other NYC neighborhoods. I have several neighbors that I consider actual friends.

There're a lot of commuters that come out of the subway and leave their trash all over the streets, the neighborhood could definitely be cleaned up near where there're high amounts of traffic whether it's foot or car.

I live in Kew Gardens now, but have lived other places and can say it is much quieter and safer than others. However, in the last few years, this nice safe neighborhood has taken a very minor dip on the not so safe end but that’s more towards the courthouse area of the neighborhood.
Everyone is super friendly and the type of people to wave at you. The Overlook park is very small, but very nice and the forest park trail is very nice.
Amazing, quiet, and close to Manhattan. Take a quick trip on the E/F train or an 18 minute LIRR ride to Manhattan.

I have never been cat-called here and no one has said anything anti-gay toward me or my spouse which unfortunately was not my experience in other neighborhoods. I feel that the people are much more down-to-earth here compared to some other NYC neighborhoods.
If you live in town, it’s conveniently near the LIRR and the subway.

voices.excerpt: Specifically where I live it is pet friendly which is important as I have a dog. I also live next to a park overlooking the water and that is peaceful.
I love that I have access to many stores, Starbucks, Dunkin Donuts, Chipotle and supermarkets, and the fact that there is a good selection of restaurants.
Good experience in New Rochelle, a big city with everything I need but also quiet suburban areas that are amazing to live.
Best part of NR is it's a short commute to the city, but if you don't need that, consider other towns farther away and your budget will go farther.

The dependence of technology also affects this, so working together to create interactive events and form new relationships would help New Rochelle become a strong tight knit city.

voices.excerpt: Bedford Stuyvesant has become a more community-involved area with tons of rally’s and group organizations being more present to stand for certain change, such as gun violence and tackling crime around the neighborhood and the city as well.
I also think the parks could use upgrades, better maintenance and more modern facilities would really improve the quality of life for residents.
Nice Neighborhood before the pandemic, nice coffee shops friendly neighbors and overall nice place to live.

There are a lot of renovated homes, and prices have been rising quickly, with some houses going for over a million dollars. This is changing the neighborhood and making it harder for long-time residents to afford living here.

Bed-Stuy is a neighborhood filled with character, and truly feels like more of a community than any other neighborhood I've lived in throughout my seven years residing in New York City. People are friendly, caring, and devoted to keeping the neighborhood a welcoming place for residents and guests, alike.
My biggest issues are how far away the subways are and how few choices of markets I have to go to compared to manhattan.
I love living in Bed-Stuy, it's such a community driven neighborhood and it has so many opportunities to engage with locals. It really strives to create a safe and friendly atmosphere.
When going to the beach or having out with my friends, I was always the one who had the longest commute time.

voices.excerpt: Kingsbridge is a very safe neighborhood. You can literally walk at 1 am and feel safe because the crime rate is very low.
It’s very open and have many options to be outdoors: Van Cortlandt Park; Mosholu Parkway; walks around the Jerome Park Reservoir; Woodlawn Cemetery; and the New York Botanical Gardens.
The low density of restaurants in Kingsbridge Heights helps keep the rat population under control.
Its a great area and peaceful. It does get noisey due to college students from time to time but I dont mind the liveliness.
Although we may face issues, our love for our community shines through it all and we are able to create memories that have shaped each and everyone in their own way.
Fordham is one stop away in the train/bus and has so many stores and places to eat/shop.
Growing up in the Bronx has this stigma of violence and anarchy, but that isn't the picture for all of its residents.
Kingsbridge has a lot of parks, stores, and different methods of transportation.
I also feel like my community doesn't have anything to offer to its residence like maybe a place local families can come together and collaborate to create events for children.
My community does not have a very good community center, although we have one I feel like maybe we can add a few more.
its aight i dont like the hill. some stores but not a lot of big chain stores. easy access by 4 D 1 trains

parking_rules.summary: Many NYC streets have alternate side parking (ASP) for street cleaning; days and hours are on the signs for each block. You cannot park on the side being cleaned for the whole posted time, even after the sweeper has passed.
parking_rules.quote: You cannot park on the side of the street that is being cleaned when ASP rules are in effect. The rules apply for the length of the entire block, and for the entire time posted on the sign, even if the street sweeper has already passed.

parking_rules.summary: ASP is not in effect on Sundays, and is suspended on listed legal and religious holidays, in severe weather and in emergencies.
parking_rules.quote: ASP rules are suspended on certain legal and religious holidays each year, during severe weather, and for emergencies. On Sundays, ASP is not in effect

parking_rules.summary: The city may suspend ASP for snow or emergencies, sometimes announced late in the day; ASP is restored after a snowfall so plows can clear the curb lane. No citywide snow-route parking ban was found on the pages read.
parking_rules.quote: NYC may suspend ASP regulations because of inclement weather or emergencies. The decision is sometimes made late in the day since weather patterns can change fast. NYC restores ASP regulations after a snowfall.

parking_rules.summary: No citywide overnight street-parking ban appears on NYC DOT's parking pages; what applies is whatever the signs on the block say, and the most restrictive sign wins.
parking_rules.quote: If there is more than one sign posted for the same area, the more restrictive one is the one in effect. If a sign is missing on a block, the remaining posted regulations are the ones that are in effect. Please check the entire block and read all signs carefully before you park.

parking_rules.summary: All of NYC is a tow-away zone: a car parked illegally, or with a missing or expired registration or inspection sticker, may be towed.
parking_rules.quote: All of New York City is a designated Tow Away Zone under the State's Vehicle and Traffic Law. This means that any vehicle parked or operated illegally, or with missing or expired registration or inspection stickers, may be towed.

parking_rules.summary: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is illegal.
parking_rules.quote: It is illegal to park within 15 feet of either side of a fire hydrant

parking_rules.summary: Meters are not in effect on Sundays or on the six major legal holidays. Other hours are on the meter or sign.
parking_rules.quote: Metered regulations are not in effect on Sundays nor major legal holidays (New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day).

parking_rules.summary: Passenger meter rates outside Manhattan's core: $2.50 first hour and $5.00 second hour in business districts such as Downtown Flushing and Jamaica; $2.00 / $3.00 in neighborhood retail districts; $1.50 / $2.50 elsewhere.
parking_rules.quote: Zone 1 - Business Districts outside of Manhattan (e.g., Downtown Brooklyn, Downtown Flushing, and Jamaica; Manhattan 125th Street) $2.50 $5.00 Zone 2 - Neighborhood Retail Districts $2.00 $3.00 Zone 3 - All Other Metered Locations $1.50 $2.50

parking_rules.summary: NYC DOT garages sell monthly permits: Court Square (Queens) $400, Borough Hall (Brooklyn) $330, Bay Ridge $275, Jerome-190th Street (Bronx) $250, Delancey and Essex (Manhattan) $600. No monthly rate is listed for the Queens Family Court garage in Jamaica.
Monthly garage permits are reserved online, first come first served, from five days before the month starts; a New York State driver's license check is run at reservation.
parking_rules.quote: Reservations open on the website five days before the first of the month at 10 am. All reservations are made for the upcoming month, on a first-come, first-served basis. A New York State Department of Motor Vehicles driver's license check is performed at the time of the reservation.

parking_rules.summary: Municipal parking fields (open lots) do not allow overnight parking; they close at the posted hour, typically 10 PM.
parking_rules.quote: Municipal parking fields do not allow overnight parking. The fields close as shown in the posted regulations for each facility. Parking after posted hours may result in a summons and leaves the vehicle at risk as there is no security at the closed facilities.

parking_rules.summary: Quarterly permits at municipal parking fields: Flushing #4 $300, Steinway #1 (Astoria) $500, Bayside $500, Brighton Beach $625, Sheepshead Bay #1 $300, Canarsie $300, Bronxdale $400.
parking_rules.quote: Bronxdale Municipal Parking Field $400 Bensonhurst #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Brighton Beach Municipal Parking Field $625 Canarsie Municipal Parking Field $300 Sheepshead Bay #1 Municipal Parking Field $300 Bayside Municipal Parking Field $500 Flushing #4 Municipal Parking Field $300 Steinway #1 Municipal Parking Field $500

dog_rules.summary: Every dog in NYC must be licensed and wear the tag in public. A license costs $8.50 a year for a spayed or neutered dog; $34 for an unaltered dog over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: All dogs in New York City must have licenses, and the licenses must be attached to their collars while in public.

dog_rules.summary: License fee: $8.50 a year if spayed or neutered; if not, $8.50 under 4 months old and $34 over 4 months.
dog_rules.quote: Licenses for spayed or neutered dogs of any age cost $8.50 per year. If your dog is not spayed or neutered, a license will cost $8.50 if the dog is under 4 months old, or $34 if it is older than 4 months.

dog_rules.summary: In any public place a dog must be on a leash no longer than six feet.
dog_rules.quote: a person who owns, possesses or controls a dog shall not permit it to be in any public place or in any open or unfenced area abutting on a public place unless the dog is effectively restrained by a leash or other restraint not more than six feet long.

dog_rules.summary: In city parks dogs must be leashed except where Parks rules allow off-leash; the Health Code lets Parks allow off-leash in unenclosed areas only within a window that starts no earlier than 9 PM and ends by 9 AM. The Parks rules themselves could not be read (site bot-walled).
dog_rules.quote: Such rules shall include provisions that prohibit unrestrained dogs in unenclosed DOPR controlled areas and facilities except during a specified range of time, that shall not begin earlier than 9:00 P.M. and not extend past 9:00 A.M.

dog_rules.summary: With proof of a current license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash in NYC Parks dog runs. The open-data list has 95 active runs (14 in Queens, 20 Brooklyn, 41 Manhattan, 15 Bronx, 5 Staten Island); see dog_parks.csv.
dog_rules.quote: With proof of current dog license and rabies vaccination, dogs can run off-leash at New York City park dog runs

dog_rules.summary: Owners must pick up after their dog in all public areas; the fine is up to $250.
dog_rules.quote: If you do not clean up after your dog, you may be fined up to $250.

voices.excerpt: Here, I’ve found that a neighborhood can be supportive without being overly social.I love the kindness of my neighbors.Everything I need is nearby, easing my transition.Residents take responsibility for maintaining cleanliness.Streets are generally well-lit, adding to the sense of safety.

Despite being an introvert, I’ve felt welcomed and supported.However, I would like to see improvements in cleanliness, more community events, better parking solutions, enhanced public spaces, and increased security measures.It has been a great place to experience how a community can influence and support an individual.
There are many shops and eateries nearby. Also, you can find many parks in the area and schools.
Nightlife is a bit bland, a few bars around but no big clubs if you wanna hit a dance floor.
Real Estate is high, there are always many houses for sale as well as apartments for rent.
We find this area a nice place to live, close to everything, transportation, shopping, dinning.
